topic: Antipsychotic physical health monitoring in children and young people

audits.title: Audit of physical health monitoring during initiation and ongoing treatment with antipsychotic medication in a tier 3 outpatient CAMHS service, Belfast
audits.standard: Belfast Trust CAMHS Antipsychotic Medication Monitoring Schedule (2015), based on CAMESA, NICE CG185, CG155 and Maudsley guidelines
audits.setting: Child and Family Clinic, tier 3 outpatient CAMHS, Belfast Trust

cycle1.result: Baseline bloods 92%; baseline ECG 75%; complete monitoring bloods 33%; physical health parameters complete 42%; schedule present and current 42% (0% on PARIS).

audits.intervention: Standardised recording using PARIS clinic letters and the schedule at the front of notes; baseline ECG mandatory.

cycle2.result: Baseline bloods 89%; baseline ECG 67%; complete monitoring bloods 44%; physical parameters complete 56%; schedule present and current 38%, present but not current 50% (0% on PARIS).

audits.other_findings: Small numbers limit interpretation; initiation checklist, bloods diary and care-pathway booklet proposed.
audits.citation: Hamlyn P, McMenamin A, Boyd H, Patton L. Audit of physical health monitoring during initiation and ongoing treatment with antipsychotic medication in a tier 3 outpatient CAMHS service, Belfast. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S323-S324. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.851.

audits.title: Audit on Baseline Physical and Metabolic Investigations Before Prescribing Antipsychotics in Children and Adolescent With Psychosis and Schizophrenia
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on baseline physical and metabolic investigations before prescribing antipsychotics in children and young people with psychosis and schizophrenia
audits.setting: West Midlands CAMHS consultants (survey of CAMHS consultant group)

cycle1.result: Indications, record keeping and nutrition/activity assessment 100%; pulse and BP 88.9%; weight and height plotted 77.8%; movement disorder assessment always 44.4%; lipid profile always 44.4%; fasting glucose and HbA1c 33.3% yes, 66.7% never.

audits.other_findings: Recommended a physical/metabolic health check proforma and re-audit after its introduction. Data were collected by questionnaire of nine consultants.
audits.citation: Javaid S, Latif L. Audit on Baseline Physical and Metabolic Investigations Before Prescribing Antipsychotics in Children and Adolescent With Psychosis and Schizophrenia. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S163-S163. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.433.

audits.title: Use of Atypical Antipsychotics as an Adjunct to the Treatment of Eating Disorders in Young People. Clinical Audit of Prescribing in the Children and Young People Eating Disorder Service Covering York, Scarborough, Harrogate and Northallerton, 2023
audits.standard: RCPsych Medical Emergencies in Eating Disorders (May 2022) and local TEWV guidelines
audits.setting: Children and Young People (CAMHS) Eating Disorder Service covering York, Scarborough, Harrogate and Northallerton

cycle1.result: Physical health monitoring 100%; blood-test monitoring 17%; medication information given 50%; unlicensed indication protocol followed 13%.

audits.intervention: Spreadsheet to monitor antipsychotic prescriptions and advice on documenting unlicensed indications and providing medication information.

cycle2.result: Physical health monitoring 100%; blood-test monitoring 100%; medication information 67%; unlicensed indication protocol 0%.

audits.other_findings: All patients were on olanzapine for distress/rumination; psychiatric follow-up and medication review were regular in both audits. Patients from the first audit were excluded from the re-audit.
audits.citation: White N. Use of Atypical Antipsychotics as an Adjunct to the Treatment of Eating Disorders in Young People. Clinical Audit of Prescribing in the Children and Young People Eating Disorder Service Covering York, Scarborough, Harrogate and Northallerton, 2023. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S268-S268. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.644.

audits.title: Clinical Audit of Use of Antipsychotics in Generic CAMHS Redcar in the Context of Baseline Investigations and Monitoring
audits.standard: NICE guidance on baseline investigations and monitoring for children and young people on antipsychotics; TEWV (2024) Psychotropic Monitoring Guide

cycle1.result: Overall compliance below 50%; side-effect assessment at 3 months 80%; ECG consideration/completion at 12 months 100%; weight, height, growth chart, waist, BP, HR, bloods and pre-treatment ECG below 80%.

audits.intervention: Recommended improved handover between teams, better communication and documentation with GPs, and agreement on where to record monitoring data.
audits.other_findings: No physical health clinic in the team; bloods and ECGs requested from GPs and results hard to track.
audits.citation: Sena Ozbal F, Egglestone L. Clinical Audit of Use of Antipsychotics in Generic CAMHS Redcar in the Context of Baseline Investigations and Monitoring. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S267-S267. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10653.

audits.title: Antipsychotic Prescribing for Behavioural Management in CAMHS: A Comparative Audit of Community and Inpatient Practice
audits.standard: NICE NG11, CG155, CG170, Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines and local Trust protocols
audits.setting: Red Kite View CAMHS inpatient unit and Leeds Community Healthcare community CAMHS

cycle1.result: Appropriate indication 100% in both. Specialist initiation 100% inpatient, 85% community. Psychological interventions tried first 77% inpatient, 54% community. Standardised behavioural rating scales 0%. Baseline movement disorder assessment 54% inpatient, 0% community. Baseline bloods 92% inpatient vs 38% community.

audits.other_findings: Community monitoring: 0% weekly weight monitoring during titration and 0% six-month liver function tests.
audits.citation: Ahmadie N, Hopkins S, Pandit C. Antipsychotic Prescribing for Behavioural Management in CAMHS: A Comparative Audit of Community and Inpatient Practice. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S289-S289. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11729.

audits.title: Compliance With NICE-Recommended Physical Health Monitoring for Children and Young People Prescribed Antipsychotic Medication Within Nottinghamshire CAHMS Head-to-Head Community Service: A Retrospective Audit
audits.standard: NICE-recommended physical health monitoring at baseline, 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6-monthly for antipsychotics

cycle1.result: Complete baseline monitoring 0% (44.4% had at least one parameter); 6-week weight 22.2%; complete 12-week monitoring 22.2%; across 25 six-monthly windows height 20.0%, weight 20.0%, BP/HR 16.0%, bloods 20.0%, waist circumference 0%.

audits.other_findings: No six-monthly window contained all recommended measures, but all patients had some ongoing monitoring and no related adverse outcomes were found.
audits.citation: Stanger F, Nair S. Compliance With NICE-Recommended Physical Health Monitoring for Children and Young People Prescribed Antipsychotic Medication Within Nottinghamshire CAHMS Head-to-Head Community Service: A Retrospective Audit. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S348-S349. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11848.
